🇮🇷🇺🇸 If Hormuz was really shut, why did oil top out near $120? The case that most Gulf crude never stopped flowing

Adrian Day, who runs Adrian Day Asset Management, sides with the administration’s claim that 65% to 70% of pre-war oil kept moving through the strait.

His logic is the price itself, because if only one or two ships a week were getting through, crude would have gone far higher than it did.

The rest of the gap was covered by the Saudi pipeline to the Red Sea, falling demand in China, and a Chinese reserve that turned out to be much bigger than Beijing admitted.

Getting back to normal is slower.

Pipelines can be repaired in months, but refineries take far longer, and Adrian says nobody will spend that money until the war has a clear end that includes the Houthis.

He adds that Nvidia was badly overvalued before its CEO scandal, and he calls the whole AI sector a bubble.
